idiom_name: one point-to-point channel + N identical consumers (receive -> process -> ack)
implementation_notes: Language-neutral form: open one point-to-point channel - an in-process queue or a brokered queue - whose delivery rule gives each message to exactly one receiver, then start N identical consumers that loop receive, process, acknowledge. The channel supplies the atomic hand-off, so the competing part needs no coordination code; what the application must supply is the policy around it: bound the queue for backpressure, cap redeliveries for poison messages, acknowledge only after processing (at-least-once), and keep every handler idempotent because duplicates and reordering are now normal. Scale the pool by starting more consumers and scale the channel by partitioning when the queue itself saturates.
code_sketch:
queue = open_point_to_point_channel("orders", capacity=100)  # in-process or brokered
for w in range(n):                     # n identical competing consumers
    consumer_loop(w):
        loop:
            msg = queue.receive()      # exactly ONE consumer gets each message
            handle(msg)                # reorder-safe and duplicate-safe
            queue.ack(msg)             # acknowledge only after handling
# scale out/in by starting or stopping consumers; producer code never changes
pitfalls: Attaching competitive consumers to a publish-subscribe channel creates N copies per message instead of N workers sharing work.
Scaling consumers before making handlers idempotent turns every redelivery into a duplicated side effect.
Leaving the queue unbounded converts overload into memory growth (or broker storage blow-up) rather than backpressure.

Wrong move: setting the visibility timeout or lease below p99 handler latency -> slow messages reappear while still being worked and a second consumer duplicates the side effects -> instead size the timeout above p99 and extend it during long work (ChangeMessageVisibility / heartbeat), and keep handlers idempotent anyway.

Wrong move: RabbitMQ automatic acknowledgement with a large or default prefetch to chase throughput -> unacknowledged deliveries are lost when the consumer dies and one greedy consumer hoards messages from its peers -> instead acknowledge only after processing and set a bounded per-consumer prefetch (basic.qos).

Wrong move: a Lambda/SQS batch consumer that performs side effects per record and commits the batch only at the end -> one failing record redelivers the whole batch and re-fires the already-completed records -> instead make each record's handling idempotent or use partial-batch responses so only the failed records are retried.
